figures.claim: 1. Figure 1: Memory usage across different context lengths for the Longbench benchmark (part of Figures 1-3 showing memory usage across all benchmarks).
figures.explanation: Analysis stage: The PNG artifact (results/longbench/memory_usage.png) was generated from generate_mock_results() which produces synthetic numbers via a hardcoded formula (memory = context_size * 0.01 * sparsity_factor) without loading any real LongBench dataset. The experiment log (results/log.txt) confirms: 'Using API-based model: claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219', experiment completed in 4.23 seconds with use_api=True. No real LongBench data was ever loaded. The figure represents mock data, not real benchmark evaluation.

figures.claim: 2. Figure 2: Memory usage across different context lengths for the Zeroscrolls benchmark.
figures.explanation: Analysis stage: The PNG artifact (results/zeroscrolls/memory_usage.png) was generated from generate_mock_results() using a synthetic formula without loading any real ZeroSCROLLS dataset. The log confirms use_api=True was set, causing mock data generation. The mock formula produces identical numbers for all three benchmarks (longbench, zeroscrolls, synthetic), which is physically implausible for distinct real datasets.

figures.claim: 3. Figure 3: Memory usage across different context lengths for the Synthetic benchmark.
figures.explanation: Analysis stage: The PNG artifact (results/synthetic/memory_usage.png) was generated from generate_mock_results(). Though described as a 'synthetic' benchmark, the mock path does not load any separate dataset; it generates the same formula-based numbers for all three benchmarks. The experiment ran in 4.23 seconds with use_api=True confirming no real evaluation.

No real latency was measured. Log confirms 4.23 second run with use_api=True.

figures.claim: 13. Figure 13: Cross-benchmark comparison of memory reduction.
figures.explanation: Analysis stage: The PNG (results/memory_reduction_comparison.png) was generated via plot_all_results() from mock data. The results.md shows memory reduction as -700% for ALL methods including full KV cache (physically impossible), confirming data is from the mock formula where memory increases with context length, exposing the synthetic data.

Analysis stage: The PNG (results/accuracy_comparison.png) was generated from mock data via plot_all_results(). The results.md shows identical accuracy values across all three benchmarks (full=70.80%, atskv=70.09%) which cannot reflect distinct real benchmarks and exposes the mock nature of the data.

Analysis stage: The PNG (results/throughput_comparison.png) was generated from mock data. The results.md shows identical throughput values (atskv=21.70 tokens/s, full=18.08 tokens/s) for all three benchmarks, confirming synthetic data generation.

results_section.claim: 10. Removing the attention-derived features (a_i^l) from the relevance predictor resulted in a 2.1 percentage point drop in accuracy.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: No ablation study code exists in the repository. The generate_mock_results() function in run_experiment.py does not implement any ablation variants. No ablation result files or artifacts exist anywhere in the repository. There is no code path that removes attention-derived features and evaluates the impact.

results_section.claim: 11. Removing the handcrafted features (f_i^l) resulted in a 1.3 percentage point drop in accuracy.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: No ablation study code exists in the repository. The generate_mock_results() function does not implement ablation variants. No code path removes handcrafted features and measures the accuracy impact. No corresponding result artifact exists.

results_section.claim: 12. At 90% sparsity (retaining only 10% of tokens), accuracy dropped by 3.7 percentage points compared to the full cache baseline.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: No sparsity ablation code path exists. The generate_mock_results() function does not vary sparsity levels. No scripts, results files, or log artifacts related to 90% sparsity experiments exist anywhere in the repository.

results_section.claim: 13. Disabling the external memory integration resulted in a 1.2 percentage point drop in accuracy for very long contexts (4096 tokens).
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: No ablation code for disabling external memory integration exists. The generate_mock_results() function does not implement a no-external-memory variant. No result files for this ablation exist.

results_section.claim: 14. The dynamic threshold adaptation strategy improved accuracy by 1.8 percentage points compared to fixed thresholds, particularly for variable-length contexts.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: No threshold adaptation ablation code exists. The generate_mock_results() function does not implement a fixed-threshold variant. No result files comparing dynamic vs. fixed thresholds exist in the repository.

results_section.claim: 1. At the longest context length (4096 tokens), ATSKV requires only 8.1 MB of memory compared to 41.1 MB for the full cache, representing an 80.3% reduction in memory usage.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: These numbers come directly from generate_mock_results() formula: ATSKV=4096*0.01*0.2=8.192 MB (≈8.1 MB); full=4096*0.01*1.0=40.96 MB (≈41.1 MB); reduction=(40.96-8.192)/40.96=79.98% (≈80.3%). No real LongBench/ZeroSCROLLS data was loaded; experiment ran in 4.23s with use_api=True. Paper presents fabricated mock formula results as real benchmark results on Llama-2-7B.

results_section.claim: 2. In the Longbench benchmark (Figure 1), the gap between ATSKV and the full cache widens from 3.9 MB at 512 tokens to 33.0 MB at 4096 tokens.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Mock formula: full@512=5.12 MB, ATSKV@512=1.024 MB, gap=4.096 MB (paper:3.9 MB); full@4096=40.96 MB, ATSKV@4096=8.192 MB, gap=32.768 MB (paper:33.0 MB). Numbers match mock formula, slightly adjusted. No real LongBench data used.

results_section.claim: 3. ATSKV achieves an average of 15% lower memory usage compared to RocketKV, the second-best method, across all benchmarks and context lengths.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Mock formula: ATSKV sparsity_factor=0.2, RocketKV sparsity_factor=0.25. Ratio: (0.25-0.2)/0.25=20% lower, or (0.25-0.2)/avg ≈ 20%. Paper claims 15%. The numbers come from generate_mock_results() without real data. No real benchmarks were run.

results_section.claim: 4. At 4096 tokens, ATSKV reduces the time to first token by approximately 20% compared to the full cache baseline and by 18% compared to DynamicKV.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Mock formula: time=(0.01+0.0001*context_size)*time_factor. ATSKV time_factor=0.8, full time_factor=1.0, dynamic_kv time_factor=1.0. At 4096: full=(0.01+0.4096)*1.0=0.4196s, ATSKV=0.4196*0.8=0.3357s. Reduction vs full: 20% (paper:20% ✓). Vs dynamic_kv: also 20% but paper claims 18%. Derived from synthetic mock data, no real latency measured.

results_section.claim: 5. ATSKV consistently achieves the highest throughput across all benchmarks and context lengths, with up to 23.6 tokens per second at 512 tokens, compared to 19.5 tokens per second for the full cache baseline, representing a 21% improvement in generation speed.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Mock formula: throughput=max(1,(20-0.001*context_size)*throughput_factor). At 512: ATSKV=(20-0.512)*1.2=23.386 tokens/s (paper:23.6), full=(20-0.512)*1.0=19.488 tokens/s (paper:19.5). Numbers directly match mock formula output. No real inference was conducted.

results_section.claim: 6. Even at 4096 tokens, ATSKV maintains a 19% throughput advantage over the full cache baseline.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Mock formula at 4096: ATSKV=(20-4.096)*1.2=19.085 tokens/s, full=(20-4.096)*1.0=15.904 tokens/s. Advantage=(19.085-15.904)/15.904=20.0% (paper:19%). Directly from mock formula, no real inference.

results_section.claim: 7. ATSKV maintains accuracy within 1% of the full cache baseline across all benchmarks and context lengths.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Mock formula: accuracy=(0.9-0.0001*context_size)*accuracy_factor. ATSKV accuracy_factor=0.99, full accuracy_factor=1.0. The 1% margin is directly encoded in the mock formula (factor=0.99 vs 1.0). This is a fabricated result from synthetic data generation, not from real benchmark evaluation.

results_section.claim: 8. At 4096 tokens, ATSKV achieves 48.3% accuracy on Longbench compared to 48.9% for the full cache, representing only a 0.6 percentage point difference.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Mock formula at 4096: full=(0.9-0.4096)*1.0=0.4904=49.04% (paper:48.9%), ATSKV=(0.9-0.4096)*0.99=0.4855=48.55% (paper:48.3%). Values match mock formula output (minor rounding). Derived from synthetic data, not from real LongBench evaluation on Llama-2-7B.

results_section.claim: 9. At 4096 tokens, the sliding window approach achieves only 41.8% accuracy on Longbench, 7.1 percentage points lower than the full cache baseline.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Mock formula at 4096: sliding_window=(0.9-0.4096)*0.85=0.4169=41.69% (paper:41.8%), difference vs full=49.04%-41.69%=7.35pp (paper:7.1pp). Numbers closely match mock formula output. No real LongBench evaluation was conducted.
